ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, the quadrilateral $ABCD$ is inscribed in circle $\odot O$. If the quadrilateral $ABCO$ is a rhombus, then what is the measure of $\angle D$ in degrees?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let $\angle ADC=\alpha$ and $\angle ABC=\beta$;\\
Since quadrilateral ABCO is a rhombus,\\
it follows that $\angle ABC=\angle AOC=\beta$;\\
Therefore $\angle ADC=\frac{1}{2}\beta$;\\
Since quadrilateral $ABCD$ is circumscribed within a circle,\\
it follows that $\alpha +\beta =180^\circ$,\\
therefore $\left\{\begin{array}{l}
\alpha +\beta =180^\circ\\
\alpha =\frac{1}{2}\beta
\end{array}\right.$,\\
From which we find: $\beta =120^\circ$, $\alpha =60^\circ$, thus $\angle ADC=\boxed{60^\circ}$.

Reasoning: Let ∠ADC=α and ∠ABC=β. Because ABCO is a rhombus formed in the order A-B-C-O, the opposite angles of the rhombus are equal, giving ∠ABC=∠AOC=β. Also because O is the center of the circle, ∠AOC is the central angle subtending arc AC, while ∠ADC is the inscribed angle subtending the same arc AC, so α=β/2. Since ABCD is a cyclic quadrilateral, opposite angles are supplementary, so α+β=180°. Combining α=β/2 and α+β=180°, we get 3β/2=180°, β=120°, α=60°. Therefore ∠D=∠ADC=60°.
